title: The Clockwork Packet
verdict: Elise Greer was responsible for the disappearance of a conductor's incident ledger.
intent: Elise Greer wanted to erase evidence of falsified delay records.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the station clerk handled both the clock key and the ledger shelf after closing.
Remove a conductor's incident ledger from its checked location.
Hide the item in a newspaper bundle tied for the morning train.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a conductor's incident ledger disappeared from a small-town train station before an audit.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the platform clock was advanced by five minutes.
The physical trace was blue paper fibers on the parcel counter.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a ticket punch with torn blue paper stuck inside.
The item could be concealed in a newspaper bundle tied for the morning train.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the station clerk could alter the platform clock and reseal the parcel counter.
distractor_cues: a conductor angry about the audit
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
